language_instruction: **Source language:** Classical (literary) Mongolian in the traditional Uighur-Mongol vertical script, printed from woodblocks (Beijing Kanjur, 1718–20). It is NOT Manchu. Columns run top to bottom and are read from LEFT to RIGHT. Transcribe in Mongolian script (Unicode U+1800 block), one source column per line, in reading order. The margin carries a Chinese section/volume/folio label. Report the primary language in the <language> tag.

ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠣᠷᠣᠰᠢᠪᠠᠢ ᠂ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ ᠤᠨ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠳᠤ ᠬᠢᠵᠠᠭᠠᠷ ᠲᠤ ᠬᠦᠷᠦᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠢ

ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠪᠦᠲᠦᠭᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠪᠦᠲᠦᠭᠡ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ ᠪᠦᠢ ᠂ ᠬᠣᠣᠰᠣᠨ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ ᠢ
ᠮᠦᠨ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ ᠢ ᠪᠦᠲᠦᠭᠡᠬᠦ ᠂ ᠪᠦᠲᠦᠭᠡ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ ᠢ ᠪᠦᠲᠦᠭᠡ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ
ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ ᠂ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠳᠤ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ ᠢ ᠪᠦᠲᠦᠭᠡᠨ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠂ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ
ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ ᠢ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠣᠷᠣᠰᠢᠪᠠᠢ ᠂ ᠪᠦᠢ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ
ᠵᠣᠬᠢᠶᠠᠨ ᠪᠦᠲᠦᠭᠡᠨ ᠪᠦᠢ ᠂ ᠂ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠳᠤ ᠪᠦᠲᠦᠭᠡᠬᠦ
ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠳᠤ ᠪᠦᠲᠦᠭᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠂ ᠪᠦᠲᠦᠭᠡᠨ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠳᠤ ᠪᠦᠲᠦᠭᠡᠨ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ
ᠪᠣᠯᠠᠢ ᠂ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ ᠪᠦᠲᠦᠭᠡᠨ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠪᠦᠲᠦᠭᠡᠬᠦ ᠢ ᠪᠦᠢ ᠄ ᠣᠷᠣᠰᠢᠭᠰᠠᠨ
ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ ᠪᠦᠲᠦᠭᠡ ᠪᠦᠲᠦᠭᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠂ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠪᠦᠢ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ
ᠪᠦᠢ ᠂ ᠪᠦᠲᠦᠭᠡ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ ᠪᠦᠲᠦᠭᠡ ᠢ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ ᠪᠣᠯᠪᠠᠢ ᠂ ᠮᠦᠨ ᠪᠦᠢ
ᠮᠦᠨ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠤᠬᠠᠭᠠᠨ ᠪᠦᠢ ᠄ ᠪᠦᠢ ᠬᠡᠮᠡᠨ ᠮᠦᠨ ᠣᠷᠣᠰᠢᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠢ ᠂
ᠡᠨᠡ ᠮᠦᠨ ᠪᠦᠲᠦᠭᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠂ ᠡᠨᠡ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠤᠬᠠᠭᠠᠨ ᠂ ᠮᠦᠨ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠪᠦᠲᠦᠭᠡᠨ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ
ᠪᠦᠲᠦᠭᠡᠨ ᠤ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ ᠢ ᠂ ᠪᠦᠲᠦᠭᠡᠬᠦ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ ᠪᠣᠯᠪᠠᠢ ᠂
ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ ᠢ ᠪᠦᠢ ᠂ ᠪᠦᠲᠦᠭᠡᠬᠦ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ ᠪᠦᠢ ᠳ᠋ᠤᠷ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠳᠤ ᠪᠣᠯᠪᠠᠢ ᠂

translation.text:
<meta>continues from previous page: the sentence begins with the dative-locative suffix -dur ("in/within"), indicating continuation from the preceding folio of the Guhyasamāja Tantra (Secret Assembly Tantra), Volume 1, Upper Part, folio 280 (page 559).</meta>
<warning>Faint red woodblock ink throughout, with slight fading along the bottom edge of several columns. The OCR exhibits some repetitive phrasing around philosophical terms like "nature" (činar), "beyond" (činadu), and "accomplishing" (bütüge-), characteristic of literal Tibetan-to-Mongolian canonical translations of Esoteric Buddhist verse.</warning>
<margin>559</margin>
<margin>Wa. Secret <note>short title for the Guhyasamāja Tantra, Mongolian: Niguča quriyanggui</note>, Volume <term>Ja</term> <gloss>the seventh volume marker in the Tibetan-Mongolian canonical ordering</gloss>, two hundred and eighty</margin>
dwelt therein; possessing the deeds that accomplish the arrival at the yonder limit of reality <note>Mongolian: "činar-un činadu kijagar", corresponding to Sanskrit bhūtakoṭi or pāramitā, the ultimate limit of reality</note>, accomplished by coming from the beyond <note>an epithet of the Tathāgata, "One Thus Come" from ultimate reality</note>:
Having conquered reality beyond, the beyond of accomplished nature, the secret
body is the body accomplished within true nature; in the beyond,
the body accomplished by coming from the beyond. Accomplish the secret
body in the beyond! In the beyond
it is arranged; accomplish it in transcendent aspiration!
The one who causes realization creates the nature of transcendent accomplishment,
and accomplishes transcendent deeds.
Having accomplished, it is the nature that accomplishes the beyond of reality.
The Victorious One <term>Ilagugsan</term> <gloss>Bhagavān or Jina, a title of the Buddha</gloss> accomplished within the accomplishment of the beyond of reality:
In the <term>śāstras</term> <gloss>treatises and canonical commentaries</gloss>, it is accomplished through accomplishment; in the accomplishment of
accomplishing, it has come to be. Saying, "This very truth has dwelt herein,"
having become reality in the beyond, it was accomplished therein:
It shall accomplish that very truth, and it shall accomplish the accomplishing;
it is accomplishing. In the nature that accomplishes the beyond of reality, within the accomplishing
nature, there is the accomplished nature of accomplishment. To accomplish the true
nature of <term>śūnyatā</term> <gloss>emptiness, Mongolian: qoosan činar, the absence of independent inherent existence</gloss>, within the accomplishment of the accomplishing nature,
reality, within the accomplishment of the transcendent nature, reality
dwelt within reality itself; within existing nature
it arranges and accomplishes. Transcendent accomplishing
was accomplished beyond; in the accomplishment, within the transcendent accomplishment
it is; within reality, it is the accomplishing in the accomplishment: the abiding
nature accomplished the accomplishment; in reality, there is the existing nature,
and the accomplishing nature has become the reality of accomplishment; that very truth is,
and within that very truth is wisdom <term>uqagan</term> <gloss>vidyā or prajñā, spiritual intelligence and insight</gloss>: as FOR that which abides as "it is,"
this very truth was accomplished; herein is wisdom, and within the accomplishment in that very truth,
the nature of accomplishment has become the accomplishing nature;
possessing reality, in the existing accomplishing nature it has become transcendent,
and the accomplishing nature has been accomplished within the transcendent accomplishing nature,
<margin>Secret Sutra <note>Chinese: Mimi jing, referring to the Guhyasamāja Tantra</note>, Volume One, Upper Part, two hundred and eighty</margin>

<summary>This folio from a bilingual Mongolian-Chinese woodblock edition of the Guhyasamāja Tantra (Secret Assembly Sutra, Volume 1, Upper Part, folio 280) presents dense esoteric Buddhist verse on ultimate reality (činar), emptiness (qoosan činar), and ritual-meditative accomplishment (bütüge-). The passage meditates on how the "secret body" of the Victorious One (Buddha) is realized through transcendent wisdom and the union of emptiness and accomplishment.</summary>
<keywords>Guhyasamaja Tantra, Secret Sutra, Mongolian Buddhism, Vajrayana, emptiness, sunyata, secret body, Tathagata, Victorious One, accomplishment, ultimate reality, woodblock print</keywords>
